newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST - Coal unit seen fuelling JCI yr shr.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Coal unit seen fuelling JCI yr shr.

text.p: A strong contribution by its unlisted coal unit, Tavistock, is likely to fuel JCI's year profit, pushing it up about 30 percent, analysts said on Friday.

Analysts polled by Reuters ranged JCI's equity accounted earnings per share for the year ended June 30 between 239 cents and 268 cents, with consensus at 251.7 cents. Last year JCI posted equity accounted earnings of 192 cents per share.
Dividend was seen between 60 cents and 80 cents per share after the group declared a 40 cents maiden dividend in the second half last year.
JCI is due to post results on Tuesday.
"If anything results will surprise on the upside, but the difference will be at least 30 percent. There's nothing wrong with that," said an analyst who asked not to be identified.
"I expect better results on the coal side. I'm looking for a big increase in Tavistock. The big number this year is going to be Tavistock," said another analyst.

The decline in the rand against the dollar would boost export earnings and increased dividend income from other units -- particularly Consolidated Metallurgical Industries (CMI) -- would bolster income, analysts said.
CMI posted attributable income for the year ended June of 169.3 million rand from 100.49 million rand previously.
"JCI's dividend income will be up as a results of better numbers. Amplats will be up and Western Areas will be up nicely too," one analyst said.
But analysts said income from gold operations would likely be pretty flat, despite the better rand gold price.
JCI was last trading 50 cents or 1.23 percent higher at 41 rand, with a volume of 31,000 shares changing hands.
